newsitem.title: USA: FIA head says adequate audit trail in Chicago pits.
newsitem.headline: FIA head says adequate audit trail in Chicago pits.

text.p: Several futures industry officials recently told the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) that both Chicago exchanges had adequate audit trail systems, challenging recent findings by the CFTC.

Larry Mollner, chairman of the Futures Industry Association and executive vice president of Dean Witter Reynolds Inc, said in an interview with Reuters that he and seven other futures industry officials argued against the conclusion in the CFTC's audit trail review.
"I don't doubt the accuracy of their work, but I do doubt the conclusion," Mollner said. "The numbers may be in favor of New York, the practical users of the market will tell you Chicago is better."

In August, the CFTC said both the CBOT and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) had audit trail systems that failed to meet the 90-percent accuracy standards mandated by the Futures Trading Practices Act of 1992.

"My comment in front of the commissioners a couple of weeks ago was all you have to do is ask the brokers -- survey all of my 350 brokers -- and ask them where they think they get the best fills," Mollner said, of his meeting with CFTC commissioners, including the new chairman Brooksley Born.

The CFTC said both exchanges must provide a plan by October 28 on how they will meet the standards, which go into effect on January 1, 1997. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
